conventions.convention: Sequential, erased-index-only, derived basis-query, and historical preprint-delimited access are distinct profiles. Index emission is charged and index tapes are erased after use; no general equivalence between profiles is assumed.

Machine acceptance is strictly greater than one half on members and at most one half on nonmembers. MajSAT and both MajMajSAT quantifiers use at least half. Plain MajSAT encodings embed identically into MajMajSAT with one implicit unused outer variable; malformed encodings are rejected.

The adopted quantum model charges every work operand and native-query endpoint toward maximum work extent, including probability-zero branches. Endpoint charging is expressly a local clarification of the source model, whose erased-index mechanism was checked in [VMW §2.3](https://theoryofcomputing.org/articles/v008a001/v008a001.pdf).

Arithmetic inputs are explicit tuple-addressed bit arrays with dimensions supplied to the uniformity machine. Addition is DLOGTIME-uniform; multiplication is logspace-uniform. Arbitrary effective encodings receive no such resource guarantee.

Optimization fixes the alphabet, ancilla policy, equivalence relation and selected cost coordinate. Whole-circuit phase equivalence does not authorize phase substitution under a control. Minimum-layer depth is distinguished from explicitly written depth.

The factor-nine routing bound concerns the unoptimized QSD construction in a contiguous interval layout, endpoint multiplexor targets, adjacent terminal blocks and both adjacent CNOT orientations. It is a gate-count bound.
The optimized QSD formula applies for n≥2; n=1 requires zero CNOTs, and an exact zero-wire circuit realizes only scalar 1. Arbitrary one-qubit gates remain a separate resource.
The almost-all Boolean-function bound fixes a nonempty finite alphabet of arity at most three, zero-initialized ancillas and one measured output bit, with no free classical acceptance predicate.

Effective gate factorization is an existence result for each fixed finite transition family. Its finitely many zero tests, branch choices and positive conditioning bounds may be hardcoded; it does not decide equality of varying Cauchy-name inputs.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the separate access profiles, strict-majority PrTIME/PrTISP classes, linear counting hierarchies for sequential and derived basis profiles, and at-least-half majority-formula languages with explicit encodings.
For sufficiently constructible t,s≥log n, the published VMW model with charged operand extent satisfies BQTISP(t,s) ⊆ PrTISP_basis(t polylog t, s+polylog t).
For either fixed profile P∈{seq,basis}, every real d and every ε>0, there is c>1 such that MajMajSAT∉PrTIME_P(n^c) or MajSAT∉PrTISP_P(n^d,n^(1−ε)).

For either fixed sequential or derived-basis profile, LCH₁ reduces to MajSAT and LCH₂ reduces to MajMajSAT with near-linear output length, polylogarithmic-time/logspace isolated bit generation, and polylogarithmic-overhead sequential on-demand generation in the stated explicit encodings.

Under the stated polynomial bounds and polylogarithmic-time/logspace generators, a derived-basis run of clock T and operand extent below M on generated input y(x) has an exact index-only simulation taking O((n+T+1) log^O(1)(n+2)) time and O(M+log(n+2)) work extent.

For an explicitly coded derived-basis machine and external clock b≥n, a fixed finite-head index-only interpreter preserves acceptance, rejection and timeout probabilities within the displayed polynomial-description/polylogarithmic time bound; it does not preserve smaller source space.
For constants α>1 and 0<β<1 there is a finite τ(α,β) such that PrTISP_P(n^α,n^(1−β)) ⊆ LCH_P,τ for either fixed profile P∈{seq,basis}.

Each member of a fixed finite polynomial-Cauchy one-qubit unitary family can be compiled projectively to rational error ε into F,F*,H, with expanded length, bit time and workspace polynomial in log(1/ε) plus its encoding length, using no additional quantum workspace.
For n≥2, the exact no-ancilla contiguous recursive QSD uses four smaller unitaries and three multiplexed rotations per nonterminal node, with c₂≤3 and c_n≤4c_(n−1)+3·2^(n−1)≤(9/16)4^n−(3/2)2^n.

Encoding and malformed-code conventions. Consumers correctly supply separate explicit encodings and resource analyses.

Arguments of unit-modulus diagonal entries in QSD demultiplexing.

Converting the final state-vector error into an acceptance-probability error.

concerns.concern: Proof 2.1 instructs: “For the opposite ordered orientation, reflect the wire labels j↦k−j in this construction and reverse every adjacent CNOT arrow.” Taken as two operations, this reverses the orientation twice. At k=2, S₂=(0→1,1→2); label reflection followed by arrow reversal gives (1→2,0→1). Squaring this sequence fixes input 001, whereas the claimed opposite remote CNOT 2→0 sends 001 to 101. I checked this basis-state computation directly. The intended mirrored construction is readily recoverable, but the stated instruction needs clarification.

seams_checked.note: Checked the supplier statements and relevant finite-bit proofs against density, base-net and compiler uses. Algebraic lifted gates, target Cauchy complexity, tolerance encoding and projective-phase restrictions are retained.

Ordered supports, later-on-left chronological products, gate occurrences, explicit depth and charged width agree with their consumers. The optimization definition separately identifies minimum-layer depth.
The rewrite rules use the exact H,T,T†,CNOT matrices and identical ordered supports. No controlled access, phase deletion or global optimality follows from those cancellations.

Checked QSD, demultiplexing, multiplexed rotations, multicontrol constructions and effective-factor uses against supplier statements. Optimized and unoptimized counts, exact phases, ancilla return and the absence of numerical synthesis-time guarantees remain distinct.

Clean workspace requires exact return for every data vector; dirty workspace requires the full tensor-identity contract. Resource composition and the multicontrol comparison preserve those requirements.

The counting lower bound uses the acceptance thresholds and finite output-law interface without importing uniformity or free postprocessing. The optimization task faithfully distinguishes minimum-layer depth from declared depth and keeps cost coordinates separate.
